item.title: Re: Medicine is difficult—there are no shortcuts
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Prof Elder's Opinion article attempts to highlight all the reasons why medical practice always has and always will remain hard. In my estimation, two major reasons have been left under-explored or completely neglected. The term "diagnosis" appears five times in Prof Elder's piece. item.title: A European perspective on equity in medical education equity from admission to specialty allocation
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Mahase reports a “broken” student finance system in England in which junior doctors graduate with very large debts, accrue interest while still studying, and then repay for decades, with predictable consequences for life choices and for social diversity in the profession (1).
